# Part IV. Risk, Experience, Time, and Self-Control {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes here

A probability is not yet a decision. Outcomes must be valued, uncertainty may be known or ambiguous, and the same consequence can feel different as a gain, a loss, a description, or a lived sample. Time then separates action from consequence. Repetition adds a final complication: a learned cue or urgent feeling can take control before a considered plan is consulted.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What would expected value and expected utility require?
- Which reference point turns an outcome into a gain or a loss?
- Is the decision based on description, experience, or both?
- What besides pure impatience makes a delayed outcome lose weight?
- Which cue has learned to trigger the behavior, and can an urge be observed without becoming an instruction?
